subgroups.name: solve 1

steps.hints: ❓ Did you change the value box in the [set sprite x to] block?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ Which value determines where a sprite is positioned horizontally (left and right)?

❓ Which value determines where a sprite is positioned vertically (up and down)?


Solution: 

The value in the [set sprite x to] block’s dropdown menu should be changed from “y” to “x”.
steps.instructions:
When the project runs, the projectiles only fall along the left side of the screen. 


Fix the bugs in the code so that the projectiles fall from the top across the entire width of the screen.

Oh no - these programs aren’t working! Problems in code are called bugs. Find and fix the bugs in the code in each section!


Help your Player earn points by collecting hearts and avoiding the blasts!

validationItems.failureText: Check the type of value in the projectile’s [set sprite x to] block.

subgroups.name: solve 2

steps.hints: ❓ Did you change the value in the [% chance] block?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ How likely is there to be a heart on the screen? 

❓ If you want there to be a smaller chance for a heart to appear, should you change the percentage to be higher or lower? 


Solution: 

The value in the [% chance] block should be changed from 80 to a number (reasonably) less than 80.
steps.instructions:
When the project runs, the game is too easy! There are too many hearts to catch, and not enough blasts to avoid. 


Fix the bugs in the code so that there is a smaller chance that a heart will appear on the screen.

subgroups.name: solve 3

steps.hints: ❓ Did you check where the [if true then] and [game over] blocks are in the code?
steps.senseiHelp:
❓ Why do you think the game doesn’t end when the Player has a score of 7?

❓If you want the game to repeatedly check the score of the game when a certain event happens, where might be a better location for the [if true then] container?


Solution: 

The [if true then] and [game over] blocks should be moved from the [on start] container block to the [on sprite overlaps sprite] container block.

﻿
steps.instructions:
When the Player earns 7 points, the game doesn’t end like it’s supposed to.


Fix the bugs in the code so that once the Player has a score of 7, the game ends and the Player wins.

Help your Player earn points by collecting hearts and avoiding the blasts!

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 3 of Yellow Belt! In this level, you’ll learn about conditionals, which are code that makes a decision in a program. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 3:

badges.title: What if?
badges.description: Use conditionals to make different things happen in a project.

badges.title: To Be or Not to Be?
What are the Chances?
badges.description: Use probability in a conditional statement.

badges.title: Same Difference
badges.description: Compare two values in a conditional statement.

badges.title: Coming from Left Field
badges.description: Launch a projectile from the side of the screen.

badges.title: Weighing the Options
badges.description: Use an if/else statement in a project.
